# CLI reference

<!-- GENERATED by tests/gen-cli-reference.py from the commands' --help. Do not edit:
     run `python3 tests/gen-cli-reference.py` after changing a help text. -->

`aicf` is the single entry point (`bin/aicf`; on Windows `bin\aicf.ps1`, PowerShell 7).
Every argument after the command is passed to the script behind it unchanged.
This page is the verbatim `--help` of each command; `<factory>` stands for the
folder you cloned AICodeFactory into.

On Windows, PowerShell binds a single-word switch such as `--yes` to `-Yes`, but not a
multi-word one: write `-DryRun`, not `--dry-run` (see
[Windows specifics](../how-to/windows.md)).

Commands: [`init`](#aicf-init), [`sync`](#aicf-sync), [`update`](#aicf-update), [`doctor`](#aicf-doctor), [`setup`](#aicf-setup), [`uninstall`](#aicf-uninstall), [`projects`](#aicf-projects).

## `aicf`

```text
Usage: aicf <command> [options]

Commands:
  init <name> [--tracked]   create a sibling project, git-init it and install the AI files
  sync [<dir>] [options]    refresh one project's AI files from the templates (default: .)
  update [options] [<name>] refresh every sibling project (a preview unless --yes)
  doctor [--yes | --json]   check this machine and its code root; --yes fixes what it can
  setup [options]           set this machine up: global skills, hook, markers, profiles
  uninstall [--yes]         undo setup on this machine (a preview unless --yes)
  projects [--open]         page: which projects are bootstrapped, which skills each one uses
  help                      print this text
  --version                 print the version

`aicf <command> --help` prints that command's options.
```

## `aicf init`

```text
Usage: aicf init <project-name> [--tracked]
```

## `aicf sync`

```text
sync-ai-templates.sh — shared engine that keeps one project's AI-instruction files in step
with this template repo. NO SYMLINKS: every file is a plain copy, so the result is identical
on macOS, Linux, Windows (Git Bash) and in server-side clones that never see this repo.

  pointer files  (manifest [POINTERS])     copied whenever they differ from the template
  living docs    (manifest [LIVING_DOCS])  created once, then owned by the project
  obsolete files (manifest [OBSOLETE])     removed (guarded entries only when unmodified)
  git hooks      (manifest [SHARED_HOOKS]) every mode but tracked, into .git/hooks (untracked)

Project modes: tracked (default — the code repo commits everything), private (--private-layer),
shared (--shared), team (--private-layer on a repo with other authors). The mode is the first
line of the managed block in <git-common-dir>/info/exclude ("# ai-templates: <mode>" …
"# ai-templates: end"); without one, the legacy .gitignore markers ("# ai-templates: private AI
docs" → private, "# ai-templates: local-only" → shared); else the code root's registry; else
tracked.

Code root: the folder holding the project (the parent of its git top level) when it holds
.ai-root/ or .ai-context-remote. Its .ai-root/ is a git checkout of the owner's private root
repo: projects/<name> records each project's mode ("mode=" and "origin=" lines; matched by
folder name, else by normalized origin), written and pushed when --private-layer or --shared
applies (lock, rebase, a commit of that file alone, never on --dry-run); it also holds
private-terms.txt and dev-context/ (the only place the engine reads them). The hidden repo's remote and owner-emails
come from the nearest folder above the project holding either (Root/group/proj finds Root).

Usage (standalone):
  sync-ai-templates.sh [<project-dir>] [--dry-run] [--commit] [--quiet] [--pull] [--agents] [--skills] [--shared|--private-layer]
  sync-ai-templates.sh [<project-dir>] --ai-context-sync [--quiet]
  sync-ai-templates.sh <code-root> --root-sync [--quiet]
  sync-ai-templates.sh [<project-dir>] --scan-private [--history]
  sync-ai-templates.sh [<project-dir>] --global-hook
    --dry-run   print the plan, write nothing
    --commit    commit only the files this run changed (paths-only commit — other work in
                the project stays untouched and uncommitted)
    --quiet     hook mode: print one line when something changed, nothing otherwise.
                A project that has a dev-context pack also prints one
                `ai-sync: dev-context` line (see below) — that line is not a file change.
    --push      after --commit, push that commit when the branch has an upstream. Off by
                default and never enabled by the session-start hook: pushing is the user's
                call, not a side effect of opening an editor.
    --pull      `git pull --ff-only` of this template repo (and the overlay) FIRST, so this run
                uses the latest templates: only when its working tree is clean, and bounded —
                after $AI_SYNC_PULL_WAIT seconds (default 10; offline, slow network) the pull
                carries on in the background and this run uses what is on disk. When the pull
                moved the repo, the engine re-runs itself so the new engine applies too.
                Before that, once per run: the code root's .ai-root, fast-forwarded the same
                way and pushed when it is ahead (a registry commit whose push failed).
                Every network step of a run (these pulls, the .ai-root push, the hidden repo's
                ls-remote, fetch and push) shares one budget of $AI_SYNC_NET_BUDGET seconds
                of waiting (default 30), the re-run included; the local work between them
                does not count. After the first step that timed out, the rest are skipped.
    --agents    also carry the template's generic AGENTS.md sections into the project
                (bootstrap-ai/scripts/refresh-agents-sections.py: only sections never
                customized, plus a missing ## Taste scaffold; shared projects and an AGENTS.md
                with uncommitted edits are left alone; in a private or team project the file
                is edited but never committed to the code repo). Needs uv or python3, else a
                no-op.
    --skills    refresh the global skill folders (~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills, …)
                from skills/ — symlinks on macOS/Linux, copies on Windows
                (override with AI_SKILLS_MODE=copy|link)
    --shared    turn the project into a SHARED project (a repo other people clone): pointer
                files become local-only — gitignored under the "# ai-templates: local-only"
                line and untracked (they stay on disk). Needs an empty index; with --commit
                the switch is one commit. Later runs see that line and keep it that way.
                Shared projects also get the private-terms pre-commit hook (see
                git-hooks/pre-commit.sh.template): a commit adding one of the owner's private
                terms is refused. The list lives outside every repo — $AI_PRIVATE_TERMS_FILE,
                <code root>/.ai-root/private-terms.txt, ~/.private-terms.
    --private-layer  turn the project PRIVATE: the owner's personal AI layer leaves the code
                repo. Layer B (living docs except .env.example, docs/state/, docs/plans/,
                config.local/, .claude/memory/) is versioned in a hidden repo instead; layer C
                (every [POINTERS] file, .claude/, CLAUDE.local.md) is rebuilt from the
                templates. Both are listed in the managed block of .git/info/exclude (anchored
                paths; config.local/ at any depth), never in .gitignore, which keeps only .env,
                .claude/settings.local.json and CLAUDE.local.md. The switch removes the legacy
                marker lines and the paths the engine listed under them from .gitignore (no
                other line), and untracks the B and C paths git still tracks (files stay on
                disk). Needs an empty index; with --commit it is one commit, "chore: move the
                personal AI layer out of the repo (private layer)". A later plain run keeps the
                block fresh and says when git still tracks a layer path. Private projects get
                the private-terms pre-commit hook too.
                TEAM instead of private when the repo's history (last 2000 commits) holds an
                author outside <code root>/.ai-root/owner-emails and its user.email (bots
                ignored; see _team_classify): its tracked files stay exactly as they are —
                never written, untracked or committed, .gitignore never gets a line — and the
                block lists only the B and C paths it does not track (plus .env when nothing
                ignores it yet). The switch commits only the legacy .gitignore cleanup, if any.
                The hidden repo (.git/ai-context, branch <root>/<project>) is committed, rebased
                and pushed by every later run to the owner's private remote —
                $AI_CONTEXT_REMOTE, else <code root>/.ai-context-remote, else
                ~/.ai-context-remote (legacy; install-global writes the root's); none = local only.
                Under a work root (_is_work_path) only the root's file counts: $AI_CONTEXT_REMOTE
                can only disable it, ~/.ai-context-remote is never read, a github.com URL is
                refused (one line each; local only). A fresh clone on another machine gets the
                docs back at its first run. The switch pushes the hidden branch first: until
                the remote has it, the code repo is left exactly as it was (one line; re-run).
                Safety rules of the hidden repo: see ai_context_sync and _aic_commit.
                Memory (private and team only): .claude/settings.local.json gains
                autoMemoryDirectory, an absolute forward-slash path to
                <project>/.claude/memory. Once per machine, after the hidden repo is
                restored, ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory is imported (missing files
                copied, differing ones under imported-<host>/, MEMORY.md union of lines).
                A tracked project gets no key, nor a team repo tracking settings.local.json.
                See _memory_settings and _aic_import_memory.
                Conformance (no network; a --private-layer / --shared switch is already the
                fix): in a code root the expected mode is the registry's, else private, and
                team conforms; the right mode with layer files still tracked does not. A
                miss prints one ai-sync: line with the switch command, in --quiet too.
                Syncing this template repo names this root's non-conforming projects and
                only counts a sibling root's. See _conform_line.
    --private-docs  alias of --private-layer (its former name).
    --ai-context-sync  sync nothing else: only that hidden repo (the Stop hook's call).
    --root-sync  sync nothing else: <code-root>/.ai-root alone, the --pull step on its own
                (bounded pull --ff-only, push when ahead, under its lock).
    --scan-private  sync nothing: check the project's tracked files against that list
                (exit 1 on a hit); --history also every commit on every ref. Before publishing.
    --global-hook  the global SessionStart hook's call (templates/global/claude-global-hook.json,
                merged into ~/.claude/settings.json by install-global; there is no global Stop
                hook). In a code root, a project whose .claude/settings.json lacks the sync hook
                (a fresh clone of a private project) gets the project hook's run (--quiet
                --commit --pull --agents --skills) when the registry knows it or it has a mode,
                else one conformance line. A silent no-op everywhere else; other flags are
                ignored. See _global_hook_plan.

Dev context (never in the project's repo): <code root>/.ai-root/dev-context/, read when it holds
rules.md or settings.json. rules.md is development rules; settings.json is optional and holds
no credentials. Scope: environment.json "label", else its "kind", else work under a work root,
else personal inside a code root (no scope, no pack — whatever the root holds).
The sync writes gitignored CLAUDE.local.md when that file is absent or already ours, and a
--quiet run prints one line telling the agent to read it. No pack: print nothing and remove a
file we wrote. An unreadable pack file
(a cloud placeholder) is one line and never fails the run.

Overlay (optional): a second repo — typically private — layered on top of this one so the
public template stays generic while personal skills, rules and configs still reach every
machine. Found via $AI_TEMPLATE_OVERLAY_DIR, then ~/.ai-template-overlay-dir, then the sibling
folder <this-repo>-private. AI_TEMPLATE_OVERLAY_DIR=none (or empty) disables the lookup
altogether — what the test suites do. Inside the overlay, the same layout applies:
  templates/<x>.template    replaces the base file of the same name (any manifest entry)
  templates/<x>.template.append  appended to the rendered file (pointers and living docs alike)
  overlay-manifest.txt      optional, same format: adds entries, or replaces the base entry
                            that targets the same destination
  skills/*                  installed with --skills; wins over a base skill of the same name
The old overlay layout (<x>.template at its root, vscode-global/) is still read, second.

Every project runs this at session start: Claude Code via the SessionStart hook shipped in
.claude/settings.json, other agents via the "Session start" step in AGENTS.md. engine/new-project.sh,
update-projects.sh, install-global.sh and doctor.sh source this file and call its functions.
```

## `aicf update`

```text
Refresh the AI-instruction files across sibling projects of this template repo — and, on
request, first bring the code root itself up to date with GitHub.

Normally unnecessary: every project re-syncs itself at session start (Claude Code
SessionStart hook / AGENTS.md session-start step). Use this for a one-shot bulk refresh —
e.g. right after a template change, on a new machine, or to migrate old symlink layouts — or
to bootstrap a project that has no AI files yet.

Usage:
  aicf update <project-name>               # refresh (or first-time bootstrap) one project
  aicf update                              # preview every bootstrapped sibling (dry-run)
  aicf update --yes                        # apply to every bootstrapped sibling
  aicf update --dry-run [name]             # explicit preview, no writes
  aicf update --yes --push                 # also push each sync commit (needs an upstream branch)
  aicf update --yes --clone --pull --push  # the whole code root, GitHub included
  aicf update --check                      # table: each repo's mode against the private-layer plan
  aicf update --migrate                    # preview the switches (no writes)
  aicf update --migrate --yes              # apply them; never pushes a code repo (--push ignored)
    --clone   clone every GitHub repo of yours (gh repo list) that has no local folder yet:
              not archived, not empty, not *-private-archive. A local folder matches by name
              (case-insensitive) or by its origin's repo name. Needs an authenticated gh.
    --pull    first fast-forward this template repo (re-running itself when it moved), then
              every git sibling that tracks a remote. A dirty tree or a branch that diverged
              from its remote is reported and left alone — never merged, never stashed.
              A preview only fetches and says how far behind each one is. The code root's
              .ai-root (the project registry) is fast-forwarded once per run, not previewed.

Each processed project also gets its generic AGENTS.md sections refreshed
(refresh-agents-sections.py: never a customized section, never a shared project).
Every run ends with a report of the repos holding commits that are not on their remote —
the one thing the session-start sync deliberately never does on its own.

Bulk runs only touch projects that already own an AGENTS.md; un-bootstrapped repos are
listed and left alone (bootstrap those explicitly by name, or with /bootstrap-ai).
Commits are paths-only, so a project with work in progress is refreshed without that work
being swept into the sync commit.
```

## `aicf doctor`

```text
doctor.sh — one command, safe to run at any time, that checks this machine's whole AI setup and,
with --yes, puts it right. It holds no logic of its own beyond the checks: every fix is the
existing scripts (install-global, sync-ai-templates, update-projects), run in the right order.

Usage: aicf doctor [--yes] [--clone] [--push] [--copy] | --json
  (no flag)  check only — one line per item, nothing written, no network:
               OK    as it should be
               FIX   wrong, and `aicf doctor --yes` puts it right
               TODO  wrong, and only you can put it right (the line says how)
               WARN  worth knowing, nothing to fix (unpushed commits, optional tools…)
  --yes      fix, in this order: fast-forward this repo (+ overlay; re-runs itself when it moved)
             and the code root's .ai-root, re-run install-global (skills, markers, global hook,
             Claude env, stale MCP entries), re-sync this repo's pointer copies, switch the
             projects that miss the private-layer plan (update-projects --migrate --yes), refresh
             every bootstrapped sibling (update-projects --yes --pull), then check again
  --clone    with --yes: also clone your GitHub repos that have no local folder (needs gh)
  --push     with --yes: also push the sync commits (never done otherwise)
  --copy     with --yes: install skills as copies (install-global --copy; Windows always copies)
  --json     the check-only pass as one JSON document on stdout (schema 1: ok, counts, checks,
             projects, unsynced) for a UI to read; alone — not with --yes/--clone/--push/--copy (exit 2)

Run it from the main checkout: in a linked worktree --yes refuses (install-global would point
this machine at the worktree).
Exit status: 0 when nothing is FIX or TODO (WARN lines allowed), 1 otherwise, 2 on bad usage.
macOS/Linux; under Git Bash on Windows it hands over to doctor.ps1 (install-global.sh is not
for Windows).
```

## `aicf setup`

```text
Installs the global AI customizations (skills, auto-bootstrap instruction) into your user
profile for every tool, and removes the MCP servers older versions registered (no MCP server
anywhere). Run once per machine; afterwards the session-start sync (`sync-ai-templates.sh
--skills`, run by every project's SessionStart hook) keeps the skill folders fresh. Re-run only
after editing ai-autobootstrap.instructions.md.

Claude Code also gets one global SessionStart hook in ~/.claude/settings.json
(templates/global/claude-global-hook.json, merged by install_claude_global_hook: other keys and
hooks kept, never duplicated). It runs `sync-ai-templates.sh --global-hook`, a no-op unless the
project sits in a code root and its own .claude/settings.json lacks the sync hook — a fresh
clone of a private project, whose layer C is not there yet. There is no global Stop hook: the
project's own Stop hook takes over once layer C exists.

Usage: aicf setup [--copy] [--overlay <dir>] [--apps-config-dir <dir>]
                 [--ai-context-remote <url>|<root>=<url>] [--work-root <name>|<path>]...
                 [--claude-profile <root>[=<config-dir>|none]]... [--claude-env <root>=<NAME>=<value>]...
  --copy            install skills as plain copies instead of symlinks (the default on
                    Windows; on macOS/Linux symlinks are live-editable, so they stay the default)
  --overlay <dir>   record a private overlay repo for this machine (see the header of
                    sync-ai-templates.sh): written to ~/.ai-template-overlay-dir and published
                    as AI_TEMPLATE_OVERLAY_DIR in ~/.claude/settings.json. Its skills are
                    installed in the same run. Without the flag an existing record is kept.
  --apps-config-dir <dir>
                    where this machine keeps the owner's personal app settings (one subfolder
                    per app, e.g. a synced "AppsSync" folder): written to ~/.apps-config-dir,
                    read by every app that follows the apps-config skill. Without the flag an
                    existing record is kept.
  --ai-context-remote <url> | <root>=<url>
                    a code root's private git remote (one branch per project, plus _root for the
                    root's own config) that carries the owner's private AI docs between machines
                    for projects switched with `sync-ai-templates.sh --private-layer`: written to
                    <root>/.ai-context-remote. <root>=<url> when the part before the first = is
                    an existing folder; else the URL is for the root holding this repo, refused
                    when that root is a work root (name it). A github.com URL is refused for a
                    work root. `none` keeps the docs in each project's local hidden repo only.
                    ~/.ai-context-remote is no longer written (the engine still reads it outside
                    a work root).
  --work-root <name>|<path>
                    mark a code root as a work root, whose private AI docs never reach a personal
                    remote: appended to ~/.ai-work-roots (one per line) unless already listed. A
                    name without / matches that folder anywhere in a path (any case); an absolute
                    path matches that folder and below. $AI_WORK_ROOTS (':' between entries;
                    none = no work roots) replaces the file; a root whose
                    .ai-root/environment.json says "kind": "work" is one as well. Repeatable.
  --claude-profile <root>[=<config-dir>|none]
                    define that code root's Claude Code profile (below): writes and commits
                    <root>/.ai-root/claude-profile.json — its config dir (default: the one it
                    has, else ~/.claude-<root name, lower case>), or none to remove it. Repeatable.
  --claude-env <root>=<NAME>=<value>
                    an environment variable of that profile's sessions (e.g. the work gateway's
                    ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL); an empty value removes it. Refused when it looks like a
                    secret (the file is committed): an apiKeyHelper or /login. Repeatable.
                    Both are engine/claude-profile-define.py, run before anything else is
                    written; the profiles are then installed in the same run.

Claude Code profiles: every code root (this one and its siblings) whose .ai-root holds
claude-profile.json gets its own config dir, ~/.claude-profiles records it, and a managed
`claude` function in the shell profiles picks it by folder (install_claude_profiles in the
engine) — e.g. the work account beside the personal one, both at once.

Root repo: for the root holding this repo and the one --ai-context-remote names, a missing
<root>/.ai-root is cloned from branch _root of that root's remote (bounded; a failure is one
line and the install carries on). An existing .ai-root is left alone.
```

## `aicf uninstall`

```text
Undoes `aicf setup` (engine/install-global.sh) on this machine, for this checkout:
  - the global skill folders it installed: links into this checkout's skills (or the overlay's),
    and copies whose .ai-template-origin names them — in every tool's skills dir and in each
    Claude profile's config dir. Skills another template repo installed, and copies without
    the marker, are not ours and stay.
  - in ~/.claude/settings.json and each Claude profile's settings.json: the global SessionStart
    hook (the entry running --global-hook) and the env keys AI_TEMPLATE_DIR, AI_CODE_ROOT and
    AI_TEMPLATE_OVERLAY_DIR. Every other key stays; a file left empty is removed.
  - the Copilot CLI block in ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md (your own text above it stays),
    the VS Code prompts file ai-autobootstrap.instructions.md, ~/.gemini/commands/bootstrap-ai.toml
  - the managed `claude` profile block in the shell profiles (~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, the PowerShell
    profiles, or $AI_SHELL_PROFILES)
  - ~/.ai-template-dir, ~/.ai-template-overlay-dir, ~/.ai-work-roots, ~/.claude-profiles and
    ~/.ai-skills-stamp, then the folders setup created that are now empty.

Never touched: any project, a code root's .ai-root and .ai-context-remote, ~/.apps-config-dir
(your apps read it), the <file>.bak backups setup kept when it removed stale MCP entries, the
"settings" a Claude profile merged into its config dir, and this checkout itself.
When ~/.ai-template-dir names another checkout, that one owns the machine-wide files: only the
skills and settings entries of this checkout go.

Usage: aicf uninstall [--yes]
  (no option)  preview: print what would be removed or edited; nothing changes
  --yes        do it
```

## `aicf projects`

```text
Usage: aicf projects [--open] [--out <file>] [--json] [--no-usage] [--doctor-json <file>]

Writes one HTML page about every project of the code root: which are bootstrapped, which still
need it (and the command that does it), and which skills each one uses. Prints a one-line-per-
project summary and the page's path. Check-only: no project is touched.

  --open                open the page in the default browser
  --out <file>          write the page there (default: ~/.cache/aicf/projects.html,
                        %LOCALAPPDATA%\aicf\projects.html on Windows)
  --json                print the page's data as JSON instead of the summary (no page written)
  --no-usage            skip reading Claude Code transcripts (no skill-use counts)
  --doctor-json <file>  read a saved `aicf doctor --json` document instead of running doctor

Skill use is counted from this machine's Claude Code transcripts (~/.claude/projects and every
profile in ~/.claude-profiles); they are read locally and never sent anywhere.
```
